facts.label: Plan

days.note: Portugal starts the trip with scenery, pastries, tiled streets, and an easy coast, not a hard city day.

spots.name: Cascais waterfront + Boca do Inferno
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · CascaisIG · Boca do InfernoFlickr

images.alt: Boca do Inferno sea arch with Atlantic water surging through the cliffs.
images.credit: Cascais source page · Google Images source

images.alt: Sunset over Boca do Inferno cliffs and the Cascais coastal platform.
Santa Marta lighthouse and Cascais harbor at soft evening light.

spots.cost: Waterfront, beaches, and Boca do Inferno are free. Lisbon-Cascais train is roughly EUR2-3 each way; taxi/transfer from LIS to Cascais often lands around $65-$110.
spots.climate: June: about 73-76 F days / 59-64 F nights. Atlantic water is chilly, roughly 62-64 F, so treat it as scenery and quick dips, not the main swim act.
spots.saveHtml: Save Stay in Cascais/Estoril and use train/taxi instead of renting a Portugal car for only two nights.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Private airport transfer to Cascais after the overnight flight; worth the ~$65-$110 if everyone is tired.
spots.restoHtml:
• Na Pizza Cascais — Margherita listed at EUR13; easy plain pizza night
  • Pasta Non Basta Cascais — fresh pasta and pizza, simple tomato/cheese fallback
  • Passione Pizza Sintra — Sintra pizza stop with plain kid-friendly orders
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lisbon Oceanarium ↩ — excellent bad-weather or jet-lag backup; current tickets are EUR25 adults/13+, EUR15 ages 3-12.
  • Monserrate Palace ↗ — lush gardens and lighter crowds than Pena; good if timed palace slots are gone.
  • Praia da Rainha ↗ — tiny in-town cove for a quick swim/photo when the open Atlantic is rough.

spots.name: Sintra: Quinta da Regaleira + Praia da Adraga
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · SintraIG · Quinta da RegaleiraIG · Praia da AdragaFlickr

images.alt: The spiral initiation well at Quinta da Regaleira wrapped in green stone.
images.credit: Trips With Rosie · Google Images source

images.alt: Quinta da Regaleira palace facade in Sintra under blue sky.
Atlantic beach and village cliffs on the Sintra coast near Azenhas do Mar.

spots.cost: Quinta da Regaleira official 2026 pricing: EUR15 adult, EUR10 youth 6-17 and seniors 65+, under 6 free. There is no combined family ticket, so a family of 4 (two adults + two kids) is about EUR50. Pena Palace is timed-entry and more crowd-sensitive.
spots.climate: June: Sintra is cooler than Lisbon and can be misty; Adraga beach is dramatic but Atlantic-cold.
spots.saveHtml: Save Choose Regaleira over a full Pena interior day; the tunnels and Initiation Well are more kid-magical and the pricing is clear (about EUR50 for the four of us).
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add Pena Palace only if you can secure an early timed slot; current rules require booking the exact day/time for palace entry.
spots.restoHtml:
• Na Pizza Cascais — Margherita listed at EUR13; easy plain pizza night
  • Pasta Non Basta Cascais — fresh pasta and pizza, simple tomato/cheese fallback
  • Passione Pizza Sintra — Sintra pizza stop with plain kid-friendly orders
spots.altboxHtml:
• Pena Palace park/terraces ↩ — more iconic color, but stricter timed entry and more crowd pressure.
  • Monserrate Palace ↗ — lush gardens and lighter crowds than Pena if the main Sintra palaces are slammed.
  • Praia da Rainha ↗ — tiny Cascais cove for an easier swim/photo if the Sintra weather is poor.

facts.label: Book

spots.name: Lisbon: Belém, Alfama & Tram 28
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · LisbonIG · BelémFlickr

images.alt: Sunrise over Lisbon rooftops and the Tagus from Miradouro de Santa Luzia.
images.credit: Amalia Bastos Photography · Google Images source

images.alt: Belem Tower reflected at sunset beside the Tagus.
Jeronimos Monastery facade under a deep blue Lisbon sky.
images.credit: Jeronimos Monastery Tickets · Google Images source

spots.cost: City wandering is free. Belém Tower and Jerónimos Monastery are timed-entry, roughly EUR8-15 adult each with reduced/free kids; Tram 28 is a normal transit ride (~EUR3) or on a 24h Viva Viagem pass.
spots.climate: June: Lisbon runs warm, about 77-84 F and hotter than the coast. Do Alfama and Belém earlier, then riverside gelato and shade in the afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride the real Tram 28 as your sightseeing instead of a paid hop-on bus, and use a reloadable Viva Viagem card for the family.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pastéis de Belém from the original bakery, or the Lisbon Oceanarium if a kid needs an indoor reset.
spots.restoHtml:
• Na Pizza Cascais — Margherita listed at EUR13; easy plain pizza night
  • Pasta Non Basta Cascais — fresh pasta and pizza, simple tomato/cheese fallback
  • Passione Pizza Sintra — Sintra pizza stop with plain kid-friendly orders
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lisbon Oceanarium ↩ — excellent heat/meltdown backup; current tickets EUR25 adults, EUR15 ages 3-12.
  • Pena Palace park ↗ — colorful terraces and forested grounds when the full interior visit feels too crowded.
  • Praia das Macas ↗ — bigger family beach with food nearby if cliff coves feel too exposed.

spots.name: Cabo da Roca, Praia da Ursa & Azenhas do Mar
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Cabo da RocaIG · Praia da UrsaFlickr

images.alt: Azenhas do Mar village perched above its Atlantic tidal pool.
Cliffs and ocean light along the Cabo da Roca coast.
Atlantic beach and village cliffs on the Sintra coast near Azenhas do Mar.

spots.cost: Free. Cabo da Roca (mainland Europe’s westernmost point) has free parking and viewpoints; Praia da Ursa is a steep unofficial scramble (not for little kids alone); Azenhas do Mar has a natural sea pool below the village.
spots.climate: June: sunny but windy and Atlantic-cold water. Great for views and tide pools, not long swims — that is what Sicily is for.
spots.saveHtml: Save Pack a picnic — there is little food at Cabo da Roca beyond one café, and the views beat overpriced snacks.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A cliffside lunch or sunset drink at Azenhas do Mar, or a short Sintra-coast e-bike stretch.
spots.restoHtml:
• Na Pizza Cascais — Margherita listed at EUR13; easy plain pizza night
  • Pasta Non Basta Cascais — fresh pasta and pizza, simple tomato/cheese fallback
  • Passione Pizza Sintra — Sintra pizza stop with plain kid-friendly orders
spots.altboxHtml:
• Praia da Adraga / Guincho ↩ — easier sand-and-café beaches if the Ursa scramble is too much.
  • Praia das Macas ↗ — bigger family beach with food nearby if cliff coves feel too exposed.
  • Lisbon Oceanarium ↗ — reliable bad-weather or jet-lag backup before the Sicily flight.
